item.title: Genomic Prediction Models for Feed Efficiency in Commercial Swine Populations
item.description:
Overview Deploying ultra-large-scale genomic associative models to identify specific single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) responsible for feed conversion efficiency.

Problem Motivation Feed costs constitute up to 70% of total swine production expenditures; identifying efficient phenotypes early is critical for sustainable agriculture.

Methodology Trained a robust Bayesian Ridge Regression model utilizing over 60,000 specific genetic markers across 10,000 distinct specimens.

Key Findings The resulting pipeline improved genomic estimated breeding values (GEBVs) accuracy by 15% compared to legacy linear methods.

item.title: Machine Learning Approaches to Early Detection of Bovine Respiratory Disease
item.description:
Overview An internet-of-things (IoT) methodology that ingests real-time biometric telemetry to catch the onset of BRD in livestock populations.

Problem Motivation BRD is the leading cause of morbidity in commercial feedlots; subjective visual observation chronically misses early-stage infections.

Methodology Deployed an ensemble Random Forest utilizing continuous stream data (rumination activity, core temperature, and movement velocity) gathered from wearable sensors.

Key Findings The model accurately triggered preemptive quarantine protocol 48 hours prior to the onset of severe, visually observable symptoms with 92% specificity.
